current_revision.mathematical_scope: Integrate Part IV local comparison to prescribed complete simplex k_L uniformly in all depth ratios, and its fixed-coordinate/reference sharpness within the local boundary-floor hypothesis class. Balanced shifted models give exact relative tensor(m/(m+b))^2Id. For L=m^2 and p=(m^2-2m,m,m), log-volume=-4b/m+O_b(m^-2), relative tensor-Id=-2b/m Id+O_b(m^-2). Thus general o(1/m) is excluded for that class, including normalized-boundary escape. No compact-projective-family lower bound or sharpness after absorbing facet shifts is inferred.

current_revision.retained_part_i_mathematical_scope: Under the existing exact-tail assumptions with nonempty boundary, the metric-ball tail recovers its exponential rate and finite coefficient W(o). Triangle inclusions give |log W(o)-log W(o′)| <= h_* d(o,o′), and a finite delta-net proves uniform convergence on every compact set of basepoints in the fixed metric-measure space. Smooth Hermitian norm changes produce uniform O(exp(-T)) Hausdorff shifts of full level sets, hence preserve Busemann phases and geometric intersection masses. Formal constant depth shifts transform coordinate density coefficients, not geometric masses. The explicitly non-KE rotational cusp has tail asymptotic 2*pi*exp(ell)*R^a*exp(-R); a>0 gives a nonintegrable vanishing tensor error and no finite normalized tail coefficient, although a bounded-additive comparison with the radial ray remains. The all-right K5 cone has two distinct minimizing chords and is not CAT(0).
